title: LSASS loads a DLL from a staging or remote location
description: Detects an ImageLoaded event for a DLL initiated by lsass.exe from a rooted profile, temporary, recycle-bin or UNC location.

hypothesis.summary: An adversary may cause LSASS to load an authentication-related or credential-access DLL from a writable staging directory or remote share.
hypothesis.rationale: A selected filename and DLL load do not prove binary identity, malicious content, signature status or injection. Process reputation and effective filesystem permissions need separate verification.
hypothesis.detection_goal: Detects an ImageLoaded event for a DLL initiated by lsass.exe from a rooted profile, temporary, recycle-bin or UNC location.

data_sources.name: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint image-load events

triage.summary: A selected filename and DLL load do not prove binary identity, malicious content, signature status or injection. Process reputation and effective filesystem permissions need separate verification.
steps: Verify the initiating executable's full path, signature and process lineage; a filename alone is not trusted identity.
Review the loaded DLL hash, signature, provenance and directory permissions, and correlate its creation with the load.
Validate any approved authentication or security product dependency before containment or rollback.
false_positives: Approved authentication or security-provider software loading a DLL from an unusual profile or staging directory.

validation.expected_outcome: Match the bounded event, key/action/path or successful operation combination; reject one-field mutations, lookalikes and absent required fields. Synthetic tests do not establish live telemetry or production performance.

limitations: A selected filename and DLL load do not prove binary identity, malicious content, signature status or injection. Process reputation and effective filesystem permissions need separate verification.
Current-revision evidence is synthetic only. Validate full generated KQL, source fields, ingestion delay, alert volume and scoped exclusions in the target before enabling.
